answers.explanation: Who are you, then what may you do. Authentication always comes first.
Cards and tokens are something you have.
Passwords, PINs, and security answers are all something you know.
Multi-factor authentication: pick 2 or more of the three factors.
Both are something you know. One phishing page can collect both, so it's still a single factor.
Something you have plus something you are: two different factors.
Role-based access: change someone's role, and their access follows.
Least privilege limits how much damage one stolen account can do.
Tripwires assume prevention can fail, and make sure someone notices. A door sensor and a file-change alert are both tripwires.
